summary: Huai-Chin Nan studied at the Republic of China Military Academy, the University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology, he taught at the ROC Military Academy and was a philosophy professor at Chinese Culture University.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed doctoral studies under Stephen F. Teiser, later serving as assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, as a professor at Zhejiang University, and as an international research fellow at the University of Tokyo.
Huawen Bai was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and served as a professor there from circa 1955 to 1996.

Hubert Decleer studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as academic director and senior faculty advisor at the School for International Training.

Hubert Durt studied under Étienne Lamotte and specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, director of the Hōbōgirin Institute, and professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart. He joined Ohio State University around 1998 as an associate professor.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Keble College. He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1930 to 1950, co-founded the Tibet Society, and was an Honorary Fellow of the British Academy and Keble College.

Hugh Gray studied at Battersea Grammar School and worked in the fields of Indology and other subjects. He served as a lecturer at SOAS University of London and the University of London from circa 1960 to 1983.

Hugh J. Silverman earned his doctorate at Stanford University. A professor of philosophy, he taught at Stony Brook University from 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature.

Hugo David earned his PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études and studied under several traditional teachers in Indology and philosophy. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge before becoming a permanent member of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.
Hugo Makibi Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kōun Yamada and held a post at Sophia University from circa 1935 to 1968.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar in the fields of sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Jing-shen Tao and traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang.
Huifeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti and held a post at The University of Hong Kong.

Huimin studied at the University of Tokyo and works in Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Taipei National University of the Arts, executive director at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and president of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Huishan Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under Kuo-wei Liu, having also studied under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under Kirill Solonin and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the doctoral supervision of Mark Allon.
